levels.name: Bellhollow Meadow
levels.brief: Four bellflowers are waiting for a drink.
levels.hint: Warm moist air meeting cold air makes rain. Draw the two fronts a little apart and the rain falls in the band between them.

levels.name: Stonebrook Basin
levels.brief: The cistern below the ridge has been dry all season.
levels.hint: Rainwater runs downhill and a stream will carry it the rest of the way. Rain high on the slope, not over the basin.

levels.name: Larkspur Field
levels.brief: Two rows of larkspur, one cold front to share between them.
levels.hint: A cold front makes rain on both of its sides. Put a warm front above and below it.

levels.name: Windmere Downs
levels.brief: Two mills, both stopped, both waiting for a breeze.
levels.hint: A wind band turns every mill it crosses. Draw it straight through both.

levels.name: Hush Village
levels.brief: Nobody has seen the rooftops in three days.
levels.hint: Strong wind clears fog, and it pushes the fog it does not clear somewhere else.

levels.name: Kestrel Ridge
levels.brief: Three mills along the ridge, and a fog bank sitting on the low road.
levels.hint: One band can serve a whole line of mills if you draw it along them, not across them.

levels.name: Coldpike Summit
levels.brief: The pike has not worn a white cap in living memory.
levels.hint: If it is freezing where the precipitation falls, rain becomes snow. Cold air alone is not enough — it needs moisture.

levels.name: Rainshadow Pass
levels.brief: The cistern sits on the wrong side of the ridge.
levels.hint: Mountains squeeze rain from moist clouds on the side the wind arrives from. Rain must fall on the cistern's side of the pass.

levels.name: Emberfield Farm
levels.brief: Bloom the border flowers. Do not touch the barley.
levels.hint: A front chills the tiles beside it too. Crops freeze if they stay cold for four beats.

levels.name: Frostgate Orchard
levels.brief: Snow on the gate ridge. Frost nowhere near the orchard.
levels.hint: Keep the cold high and far. Moisture can travel where a front should not.

levels.name: Candlewick Rows
levels.brief: Bloom the candlewick. The seed barley either side must stay warm.
levels.hint: Cold air spills one tile past the thread you draw. Leave the barley a margin.

levels.name: Marrowmere
levels.brief: The mere has drawn back from its banks. The village must stay dry.
levels.hint: Water spreads once it is deep, and it always looks for the lowest ground.

levels.name: Twin Cisterns
levels.brief: Two cisterns, one sky. Between them, eight units of water.
levels.hint: Rain that lands in the middle will find both basins if it gets deep enough.

levels.name: Sluicegate Fen
levels.brief: Fill the fen and top the cistern below it without drowning the lane.
levels.hint: A brook takes water past the tiles it runs through. Follow where it points.

levels.name: Millbrook Hollow
levels.brief: The whole hollow at once: mills turning, flowers open, the brook pool full.
levels.hint: One cold front can serve two rain bands. Rain that lands beside a brook is rain the flowers will not get.
levels._note: two cancel bands at rows 3 and 5 rain onto both flower rows; row 5 runoff drains into the pool at rows 7-8

levels.name: The Long Loom
levels.brief: Snow on the pike, water in the pool, flowers on the terrace, frost nowhere near the barley.
levels.hint: Work from the top of the map down. Everything you make runs downhill into the next problem.

levels.name: Snowmelt Steps
levels.brief: Cap the steps in snow, then let the sun send it down to the cistern.
levels.hint: Snow melts wherever the air is above freezing. Make it high and cold, then warm the slope below.

levels.name: Whitecap Tarn
levels.brief: A white cap on the horns and a full tarn beneath them.
levels.hint: Moisture can be carried to cold air instead of dragging the cold air down to it.

levels.name: Meltwater Meadow
levels.brief: The snowfield above feeds the meadow. Nothing else will.
levels.hint: Water that arrives as meltwater still counts as a drink. The flowers only need the air to stay mild.

levels.name: Thawgate
levels.brief: Snow on the gate, water in the pool, and the barley untouched.
levels.hint: Cold belongs at the top of the map. Everything you want warm should be far below it.

levels.name: Braided Gale
levels.brief: Four mills, two ridges, one stubborn fog.
levels.hint: Wind spills one tile either side of the band. Two bands can cover four rows.

levels.name: Leeward Fields
levels.brief: The flowers sit in the lee of the crag. Bring the rain over to them.
levels.hint: Wind pushes cloud one tile a beat. Make the cloud upwind of where you want it to fall.

levels.name: Turning Weather
levels.brief: Keep the mills turning while the cistern fills. Neither can wait.
levels.hint: A wind band is not only for mills. It moves your rain as well.

levels.name: Squall Line
levels.brief: Soak the marsh. The cottages on the bank must stay above the water.
levels.hint: Deep water spreads sideways. Keep the deepest part of the storm away from the bank.

levels.name: Glass Terrace
levels.brief: Flowers on the terrace, water in the trough, mills turning above.
levels.hint: Solve the highest thing first. What you make up there arrives everywhere below.

levels.name: The Cold Braid
levels.brief: Snow above, blooms below, and a hard line between them.
levels.hint: Warm and cold cancel where they overlap. That is a tool, not a mistake.

levels.name: Everything at Once
levels.brief: Mills, marsh, cistern and blooms. The hollow is asking for all of it.
levels.hint: Read the objectives in height order and weave from the top down.

levels.name: The Last Loom
levels.brief: One hollow, every rule, nothing spare.
levels.hint: There is no thread here you do not need. Place the one with the fewest options first.

collectibles.name: Rainbell Flower
collectibles.flavour: Opens only while rain is falling. Closes the moment the sky clears, as if embarrassed.

collectibles.name: Frost Fern
collectibles.flavour: Grows a new frond for every freezing night. Glitters when the terrarium runs cold.

collectibles.name: Cloud Moss
collectibles.flavour: Drinks straight from the air. Will not tolerate being watered directly.

collectibles.name: Sunlace Clover
collectibles.flavour: Turns its face through the day. Weavers say a field of it can be read like a clock.

collectibles.name: Mistcap Mushroom
collectibles.flavour: Appears overnight wherever fog has recently lifted. Never where it lingers.

collectibles.name: Wind Reed
collectibles.flavour: Sways even in still air, keeping time with a breeze that passed some days ago.

collectibles.name: Thaw Lily
collectibles.flavour: Flowers in the puddle a snowdrift leaves behind, and never anywhere else.

collectibles.name: Gale Flax
collectibles.flavour: Its fibres lie flat in the direction of the last strong wind. Weavers use it as a compass.

collectibles.name: Loomstar
collectibles.flavour: Six petals, each opening to a different condition. Nobody has seen all six at once.
